name: Tasks
description: Per-session task list. Plan multi-step work, mark progress as you go, the user sees a live TODO. Single Task tool with action switch (add, add_many, replace_plan, update, status, start, done, remove, reorder, list, clear). Prefer add_many + tasks[]. Model and human boards use canonical ordinal ids. State lives at ~/.minimal-agent/sessions/<sid>.tasks.jsonl. Current task list is auto-injected every user turn as <ma::agent::tasks>.

tool.name: Task
tool.description: Plan and track a per-session task list that the user sees as a live board. Use it for work of 3 or more steps, or when the user asks for a plan. Use `add_many` with `tasks` to plan once, then `start` and `done` with a canonical id from the board. Do not use it for trivial work of 1 or 2 steps. Do not record lessons here, because memory owns those. Do not echo the board as prose. `canceled` means abandoned and `done` means finished, so pick the verb that matches the intent. A finished phase header is `done`, not `canceled`. Returns an `OK` acknowledgement, then the updated board or a compact note, per the configured result verbosity.

action.description: What to do. `add` adds one task, and `add_many` adds a task tree. `replace_plan` replaces the board with a new plan. `update` changes a title or a status, and `status` sets a new status. `start` moves the task to `doing` and auto-starts the parent. `done` finishes a task and auto-promotes the parent when the last open child closes. A parent stays `doing` while siblings stay open. `remove` deletes a task and its subtasks. Use it for a task that never started. `reorder` changes the top-level order. `list` shows the board, and `clear` empties it. After a validation failure, retry once. Do not add duplicates one by one.

id.description: Canonical task id from the current board or latest Task tool result, such as `1` or `1a`. Required for: update, status, start, done, remove.

title.description: Task title (single line). Required for: add. Optional for: update (give at least one of title or status).

tasks.description: Preferred tree form for add_many or replace_plan, with optional depth-2 children. Each entry is `{title, children?}`, where `children` is an array of subtask titles. Mutually exclusive with `items` and `titles`. Cannot combine with `parent`. A child promotes the parent task, so do not also call `done` on the parent. Do not convert the array to a string.

children.description: Optional subtask titles under this parent (depth 2 only, strings, not nested objects).

titles.description: Flat list of task titles. Send exactly one of `tasks`, `items` or `titles`. Use `titles` for a flat plan or a batch under `parent`.

items.description: Alias of `tasks`, in the tree form `{title, children?}[]`. Prefer `tasks`. Cannot combine with `tasks`, `titles` or `parent`.

children.description: Optional subtask titles under this parent (depth 2 only, strings, not nested objects).

parent.description: Make this task a subtask of the given parent. Accepts the same shapes as `id`. Optional for: add, and for flat add_many with `titles`. Not allowed with tree `tasks`/`items`.

after.description: Insert the new task immediately after this task instead of at the end. Top-level only. Optional for: add.

status.description: New status. Required for: status. Optional for: update. `canceled` means abandoned and `done` means finished, so pick the verb that matches the intent.

reason.description: Optional reason recorded when setting status to canceled.

order.description: Top-level task ids in the desired new order. Subtasks ride along with their parent. Required for: reorder.

filter.description: Filter for `list` (currently advisory, full set is always rendered).

format.description: Result content format. `text` returns an acknowledgement plus the board when the verbosity allows it. `json` returns the same data as a parseable shape.

parallel.description: For `start`: accepted for compatibility. `start` always keeps other `doing` tasks as `doing` (no demotion).

force.description: For `clear`: override the refusal when any task is `doing`. Default false.
